_about: The spec of kitcut.ai's 'Offer ad' template (studio/templates.py make --spec): what it is, what the film keeps of its sample (keep, generic), when the sample is the person's own (identity), and its author's notes to Claude. Its film is projects/offer-ad (local: the sample's photo, product image and logo are third-party; config/templates/offer-ad/ has the code and a made-up content sample). No narration: sound is written by the film's own code. v7 (2026-10-02): made exact to the ad it recreates (the owner's screen recording of U.S. Bank's Threads ad), measured frame by frame: a 5 s loop that cuts back to the picture alone, the product and the figure in together at .35 s, each subline line sliding in whole from past the frame's right edge (1.05 s, then .32 s later), the logo on screen the whole loop, no exit; and the square's sizes off the ad at 1080 px (card 250 wide from 166 in, figure tracking +4%, subline 52, logo 190 tucked 22/40 into the corner, a 2% push-in instead of 7.5%).
title: Offer ad
description: A 5-second looping video ad for one offer, the way the big card issuers run theirs in a feed: a photo fills the frame and plays alone for a moment; the product fades in beside a giant figure (4X, 50%, $0, 2 months free) that slides in from the right; a two-weight line slides in whole under it, line after line; a button and fine print if there are any; the brand's logo sits in the corner the whole loop; then it cuts back to the picture alone and loops. Square for a feed, vertical for stories and reels. A light score and soft cues, no narration.
author: KitCut
example: Our spring sale: 30% off all running shoes until Sunday. Our logo and a photo of the shoes are attached.
brief:
A 5-second looping offer ad, 60 fps, with no narration, on a 120 bpm clock that never moves with the content (a beat is .5 s), measured off the U.S. Bank feed ad it recreates: the picture alone for .35 s (it breathes very slightly over the loop so the end meets the start); the product fades in and the big figure fades and slides in from the right together at .35 s; the subline slides in one line at a time, each whole from past the frame's right edge (1.05 s, then every .32 s); the button (if any) pops at 1.9 s; the logo is on screen the whole loop; nothing leaves -- the loop cuts back to the picture alone. It is a feed ad: it says everything with the sound off, and the score (a warm pad, a soft pluck line, a chime on the figure's beat) and the cues are written by film.js from its own clock. The film is not finished until you have called the sound tool once at the end, after your last edit to film.js or content.json: it writes score.json and sfx.json from the film and mixes them, and the studio will not take the film without them.

The frame is 1:1 (1080 x 1080) unless asked: for a story, a reel or a short, 9:16 (1080 x 1920, the product sits above the words and the layout keeps clear of the app's bars). The one film.js lays both out (its code also lays out 16:9, which this template does not offer yet); never rewrite the layout, only the content.

content.json is the whole job; film.js should almost never change. Fields:
- figure: THE number or claim, 1-8 characters as the offer writes it: '4X', '50%', '$0', '-30%', '2 for 1', 'FREE'. A longer one with a space ('2 months free') wraps onto two lines by itself; do not abbreviate it. It is the offer's own figure from the person's words or their page -- never invent, round up or estimate one.
- subline: 1-3 short lines that finish the sentence the figure starts ('off your first year', 'delivery on every order'). *Asterisks* make a word bold, everything else is light: mark the 2-4 words that carry the offer ('*delivery* on every order' / 'this *whole month*'); a line with no asterisks is all bold. Keep each line under ~28 characters; it is fitted, never cut.
- cta (optional): the button, up to ~20 characters ('Shop now', 'Start free'). Leave '' when the offer has none -- an ad with no button is fine, and the sample has none.
- legal (optional): the small print the offer must carry, one or two sentences, only what the person gave or their page states ('New customers only. Terms apply.'). '' when there is none; never make terms up.
- photo: the person's attached picture ('upload1'...) or '' for none. Look at it: choose focus [x, y] (0-1) to keep the subject in the frame in every shape (a vertical frame crops a wide photo to a column), and anchor, 'top' or 'bottom': the words go on the edge where the picture is calm (sky, wall, foliage, floor), never over a face, the product or a bright focal point such as a sun or a lamp. The film samples the photo under the words and veils it only as much as the text needs, so do not darken or edit the photo. With no photo attached, look for one before anything else -- do this every time the offer has something to see (shoes, a trip, a meal, a gym, a bank card, a ticket), and skip it only for a pure software plan or price with no visual subject: the person's own site if they gave a link, else a freely licensed photo of what the offer is about (Unsplash, Pexels, Wikimedia Commons: the picture tool, then photo: 'web_name'), a real place or object with no recognisable person unless they are the brand's own. Only when nothing fits is photo '' and the brand's colour the page, which is a real ad too.
- product: {image, round} for the thing sold -- a card, a screenshot, a bottle, a shoe -- or null when there is none (then the figure takes the width). round is the corner radius at 1080 px: 20-26 for a rectangular picture (a card, a screenshot, a book cover; the film crops it to that radius and gives it a shadow and a slow sheen), 0 for a cut-out with a transparent background (a shoe, a bottle). It is a picture the person attached; never draw a stand-in.
- logo: {image, light} from template_pictures(logo='upload3') -- it answers with the keys (logo / logo-light); the film picks the one that reads on what is behind it. Or null: then brand.name is set in type in its place.
- brand: {name, ground, accent, ink}. ground is the brand's main DARK colour as a #RRGGBB (it tints the veil over a photo and is the page when there is no photo -- a light one is fine, the words turn dark), accent is its signature colour (the figure on a plain page, the button), ink is the light word colour (#FFF8EC unless the brand's is warmer or cooler). Take them from the logo, the site or the product; name is the brand's name as it writes it.
- align: 'left' (default) or 'center' -- centre only for a frame with no product, or for the vertical frame with a product above the words.

How the person's pictures become the film's own: attach order is upload1, upload2... Put the photo's key in photo, the product's in product.image, and call template_pictures(logo='uploadN') for the logo (a logo with a solid background is keyed out for you). The sample's own pictures (sample1, sample2, sample3) must not remain in content.json: every one is replaced or removed (photo '', product null, logo null). If they attach only a logo and a sentence, find a photo as above; and with no photo and no product, a brand-coloured page with the figure huge is a real ad, not a failure.

What it must survive, and does: a figure from 1 to 8 characters or a wrapped long one; one to three subline lines; no product, no photo, no logo, no button, no fine print; a bright or a dark photo (the veil and the word colour are measured); a light or dark brand colour. Where it is tight: the subline's longest line against the column beside the product (a long line is shrunk to about half size, then wrapped), the fine print (up to three lines), and the figure when the offer is a phrase ('2 months free' wraps; 'FREE SHIPPING OVER $50' does not belong in the figure: put '$50' and say the rest in the subline).

In another language, translate the subline, button and fine print; the faces carry Latin and Cyrillic. Prices and figures stay as the offer writes them. Do not add scenes, narration, captions or extra graphics: it is one ad for one offer.
